newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Cathay, Dragonair A330 planes back in air.
newsitem.headline: HK's Cathay, Dragonair A330 planes back in air.

text.p: Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd and Hong Kong Dragon Airlines Ltd said on Tuesday their entire fleets of Airbus Industrie A330-300 aircraft were flying again after being grounded with engine trouble.
All 11 of Cathay's A330-300s had been back in the air as of Sunday after the first aircraft resumed service last Thursday, a Cathay spokeswoman told Reuters.

But four "hangover" cancellations would take effect on Tuesday and again on Wednesday because booking arrangements were made assuming the planes would not be back in the air until a later date, she said.
All flights would be back to normal on Thursday, she said.
Dragonair resumed service with its four A330-300s on Tuesday after putting the first of the twin-engined planes back in the air last Thursday, a spokeswoman told Reuters.
There was no cancellation of flights on Tuesday or "in the past few days", she said.
The two Hong Kong carriers had said they expected all their A330-300s to be flying again by last weekend.

The two carriers suspended their A330-300s on May 24 after three inflight engine shutdowns on Cathay and a fourth on Dragonair created questions about the reliability of the Rolls-Royce Plc Trent 700 engine.

Cathay said last week the problem, traced to insufficient lubrication of a bearing in the engine's step-aside gearbox, had been fixed and the airline and regulatory authorities were satisfied the modification was completely airworthy.
Swire Pacific Ltd and Cathay Pacific together hold about 26 percent of Dragonair, whose major shareholder is China National Aviation Corp (CNAC).
Cathay chairman Peter Sutch has said the groundings would slice between HK$120 million and HK$150 million (US$15.5 million and US$19.4 million) from the airline's bottom line this year.
Other Cathay officials have said the final figure would depend on a number of factors, including compensation the airline could receive from Rolls-Royce.
